chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from Manṣūr ibn ‘Abbās, who narrated that: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said:
The sacred boundary (ḥaram) of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is five parasangs from each of the four sides of the grave.

key_terms.حَرَمُ: Sacred boundary or sanctuary; a zone of honor and specific legal rulings.
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: Plural of farasang (parasang), a traditional unit of distance approximately equal to three miles or five kilometers.

ai.seo_question: What is the defined sacred boundary (haram) of Imam Husayn's grave?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the *ḥaram* (sanctified zone) of Imam al-Ḥusayn’s shrine as five *farasikh* (approximately 20-25 km) in all directions, a measurement crucial for determining the validity of specific ritual honors and prohibitions during pilgrimage. In Shia jurisprudence, this defined boundary distinguishes the sacred precincts where special etiquette applies, reflecting the theological elevation of the Ahl al-Bayt’s resting places as extensions of divine presence on earth.
